items.text: thumbnails are real frames of each scene, in its own colors, with its trails: the built-in scenes come with theirs, and a scene you make gets its own after it has played for a few seconds (an edit makes a new one). Until then its pattern stands in
every panel above the bar has its tabs and its CLOSE along its bottom edge, by your thumb. It closes by sliding down toward its button, or with a swipe down on that band; Esc still closes it
while the robot runs, its antenna sends a signal: small arcs light in turn on its beat, on the bar and in Auto play

the robot's shelf is the scenes, as small screens: the playing one lit, the next one marked with a dot (the robot now picks its next scene ahead, in shuffle too). Tap one to play it now; a running robot carries on from there. ‹ › show the same strip
the robot dances while it runs, on the bar and in Auto play: its eyes glance and its antenna light pulses, on the beat when it counts beats or bars. A steady light if you reduce motion
Auto play's big button is the robot. Every (seconds, beats, bars) is back in Auto play, and only there
the shelf hugs its controls, centred under the bar, and CLOSE runs up its right edge
Auto play fits a short window (1720 x 557) without scrolling
the bar never moves now. The bottom shelf slides up into the room under it, frosted, one row at one height for every button, with a caret pointing at its button and a Close at the far right

Sound's shelf is the sounds themselves, the five beats and the bytebeats in one row (or the water). Up top, Sound keeps mic, your file and mix, then tap, eighth, dry, links and touch; Mute is gone, a tap on the speaker mutes
the robot's shelf is Seconds | Beats | Bars and its beads in one row; the dice's shelf is how often it rolls, and that now lives only there
on a computer the shelf's controls keep their phone size; a wider window shows more of the row
Auto play's line no longer counts down or wraps, so nothing in the panel moves between stopped and playing; the panel fits without scrolling, and Every lives only in the robot's shelf
one panel above the bar at a time: Auto play and a drawer no longer open together, and the scene's name hides while a panel is up
nothing under the bar overlaps: badges, "mic" and the carets share one row, and the speaker's × says muted on its own

Water. Drag down on Sound and choose Water up top: every sound, beats and bytebeats too, as if heard through water. Six presets (Shallows, Deep, Open sea, Rain on the roof, Stream, Hydrophone) and a depth; the field moves the depth a little, and your finger stirs it
water beds with no beat: surf, stream, hydrophone, rain. The field hears them like a beat; a preset brings its own
water voices: a tap is a drop, a drag lets out bubbles, a long gesture a whale, higher on screen higher; or let the music's beats play them
all of it is made in the app from noise and tones: no recordings
after you chose a beat, the field stopped feeling its beats (the beat signal never fired again). It feels them again, so scenes linked to the beat pulse as they were meant to
every bar button reads four gestures. Tap does what it always did; drag up opens what holding opened; drag down opens its controls in a new shelf at the bottom; press and hold opens both

the bottom shelf follows the button: the robot's beads, the dice's how much and how often, a strip of scenes, still · video · GIF, the source's drive, show, zoom and turn, the sound's volume, beat, bytebeat, wet and react, and the line and ground colors
the bar sits above the shelf. ⌄ or Esc puts the shelf away; drag down on any button brings it back
the dice's up-and-down drag (how much) and the speaker's (volume) moved into the shelf; the dice's sideways drag still sets how often
no more reloads when the player is off screen

the text sequencer's timing is a row of beads, like Auto play's: 2, 4, 8, 16 seconds or a bar; a Stay | Morph switch above them sets how long a word stays or how long the morph takes, and both show under the row
In order and Shuffle are tiles, the way Auto play shows its order
case (as typed, ALL CAPS) and size (same size, each fills) are drawn icons
word rows read like Scenes: add to the sequence on the left, remove and the drag handle on the right, hairlines between; in sequence order the handle reorders the sequence
Pro keys. Settings › Pro key takes a key from the studio (or a link that carries one); Pro features that are built then work, and their locks go
with Pro, save as many beats as you like, and export and import them all
